title: Stream teardown, function-call safety, and structured-output atomicity
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We have recurring edge cases where client disconnects or request timeouts interrupt an in-progress streaming generation that includes function/tool calls and structured JSON output. Partial function-call payloads or truncated structured responses lead to downstream consumer failures (parsers, tool invokers), and complicate retries and billing reconciliation.

Objective: Implement a stream teardown protocol and runtime safeguards that ensure function-call invocations are delivered atomically (either fully emitted and committed or not visible to downstream), partial structured-output fragments are cleaned or marked consistently, and backpressure/timeout cases are handled with clear signals to clients and observability. The solution must be compatible with existing streaming clients and the function-calling compatibility shim used by legacy SDKs.

Scope:
- Server-side teardown & handoff protocol for in-progress generations that contain function calls or structured JSON tokens.
- KV-cache checkpointing and abort semantics around function-call boundaries.
- Client-facing signals (final event types) for: function_call_committed, function_call_aborted, structured_output_truncated, stream_timeout_notice.
- Graceful fallback behavior for legacy clients that don't understand new events: ensure a backward-compatible delta that doesn't break parsers.
- Unit/integration tests, migration guide for SDKs, and dashboarding for new metrics.

Out of scope: changes to underlying model checkpointing beyond KV-cache hooks, large rewrites to client SDKs (we will publish adapters instead).
acceptance_criteria: When a function call is emitted mid-stream, the runtime creates a checkpoint before invoking tool wiring so that on client disconnect we can either commit the call or produce a deterministic abort event.
Downstream consumers never receive truncated/invalid JSON for structured-output streams; if truncation occurs the final event explicitly marks the output as truncated with a stable error code.
Legacy streaming clients that ignore the new event types continue to see consistent token streams and a final error token if the function call was aborted, preserving parser safety.
Automated test suite covers: normal commit, client disconnect during function call generation, server-side timeout during a tool call, and deliberate KV-cache/commit failure paths.
Dashboard shows: function_call_commit_rate, function_call_abort_rate, truncated_structured_output_count, average teardown latency; initial SLO: function_call_abort_rate < 0.5% for P0 traffic.
Runtime telemetry includes enough metadata to reconcile billing and replay decisions (request_id, generation_epoch, commit_marker_id).
notes: 2025-02-10 Asha created the ticket after INC-2025-02 partial-function-shed incident revealed parser failures when clients disconnected during tool emission.
2025-02-11 Design sync: decided to use a lightweight commit/abort marker written to metadata store rather than a heavyweight global transaction. Action: infra to expose checkpoint hook (ENG-827001).

2025-02-12 Prototype: implemented KV-cache checkpointing at function-call boundary in a local branch. Observed 1-2ms median added latency for the checkpoint on small models. Next: add abort marker semantics and client-facing event envelope.
2025-02-14 Review feedback from PM (Miguel Torres): ensure compatibility shim for older SDKs that expect raw token deltas. Miguel: publish migration guide and a small client adapter for Node/Python.

2025-02-16 Engineering note (Liang): implemented server-side stream finalizer that emits one of: commit_event, abort_event, or truncated_notice. Added unit tests for commit->emit ordering. See PR #5820.

2025-02-18 QA: Integration tests failing for server timeout during external tool invocation (race between abort marker write and connection teardown). Repro script and logs attached to PR. Next: add retry/backoff for marker writes and a fallback synthetic abort event written to durable event log.
implementation_summary: We will add a checkpoint API at the serving layer that is invoked immediately before a function/tool call token sequence begins. The checkpoint produces a commit_marker_id persisted to the metadata store. If the model completes token emission for the function call and downstream wiring succeeds, the runtime writes a commit event; on timeout or disconnect the runtime writes an abort event and emits a truncated_notice to clients. To preserve compatibility, we will keep token deltas identical for legacy clients and append a final framed event (JSON envelope) that modern SDKs can parse. This approach minimizes changes to the tokenizer pipeline and keeps the cost of the feature low.
risks_and_mitigation: Race between commit_marker write and socket close -> mitigate with write-retry and a durable event log that can be reconciled by offline workers.
Increased latency on P99 for lightweight requests due to checkpointing -> mitigate by sampling-based checkpointing and fast-path for non-function-call generations.
SDK adoption lag -> provide adapter shims and server-side backward compatibility so older clients see safe token streams.
Billing reconciliation complexity -> include stable markers in telemetry and provide a reconciliation job (post-process) for ambiguous cases.
